title: Every device-management command at et-platform 836a4ab (BL2 0.22.0), classified READ or WRITE from the firmware source - E144's copy: command 74 group 0 classified READ from the held patch source
written: 2026-11-02 (Mon, week 45), Q136(w), desk only; docs/reports/data/2026-11-02-q136w-write-audit/README.md explains it

source.bl2_version: 0.22.0 (device-bootloaders/CMakeLists.txt:4), the version all four lab cards report since 27-31 Oct 2026; aifoundry3's 0.22.0 is a non-public build (see caveat)
source.paths: handler paths are relative to device-bootloaders/src/ServiceProcessorBL2/ unless they start with a top-level directory of the repo
source.host_library: devicemanagement/src/DeviceManagement.cc:430-560: every command goes to the service processor (SP); no command is answered on the host
source.caveat: PASS at the version-matched public source; the running binaries are not hashed (gov-prep's rule-8 residual), and no card exposes a BL2 hash, so each card runs *a* 0.22.0. One is known to differ: aifoundry3 runs a non-public build, the thermal firmware build first flashed there on 7 Oct 2026, which answers command 74 (DM_CMD_GET_ASIC_PVT_SAMPLES, absent from 836a4ab) and whose answer changed from whole degrees (7 Oct) to raw sensor codes (31 Oct) while the card reported release 1.4.0 / BL2 0.22.0 (docs/findings/14-card-behaviour.md, 'A finer reading exists on aifoundry3's firmware build'; docs/reports/data/2026-10-31-e89-heat-low-power/README.md, 'Joins and traps'). For aifoundry3 this table classifies from the nearest public source with a known divergence: a command present in both is read from 836a4ab's handler, which that build may not share. The residual binds every aifoundry3 lane (Q136: E127, E130, E132, E134). A card running another build needs its own audit.
source.corrected: 2026-11-02 (Mon, week 45), after verification: the statistics reset's second PMIC write (the 0x43 snapshot), GET_FRU's three register writes (once, not per byte), the forms of SET_STATS_RUN_CONTROL, build/ettelem-hpl/ under ettelem-dv2, aifoundry3's caveat, and the three ettelem pseudo entries; the README's 'Corrections after verification' lists them

classes.READ: No write anywhere on the card except the reply itself: RAM getters, PVT/PLL/OTP register reads, PMIC register reads. A READ may refresh the SP's own RAM copy of the value it just read; that is noted, not counted as a write.
classes.WRITE: Writes something on the card: a register, flash, persistent or RAM configuration, a counter or log setting, the PMIC (any set_pmic_reg), a reset or a power action.
classes.UNSUPPORTED: No handler at 836a4ab: the SP logs an ERROR (which raises an SP_RUNTIME_ERROR event to the host) and may never reply. Treated as NO-GO.
classes.UNCLASSIFIED: Not in the 836a4ab source. NO-GO until classified from the source of the build that runs it.

common_side_effects: Every command makes the SP log one INFO line on arrival (rtos_task/command_dispatcher.c:130). It reaches the SP trace buffer only when the SP log level is INFO or DEBUG; the boot default is WARNING (services/trace.c Trace_Init_SP default filter TRACE_EVENT_STRING_WARNING).

Every ERROR-level log line increments the SP's runtime-error counter and sends one SP_RUNTIME_ERROR event to the host (services/log.c:240-249 and :414-436; RT_ERROR_THRESHOLD is 0 at include/config/mgmt_build_config.h:379). The driver counts them (SpCeEvent). So any command that fails, or asks for an invalid state, leaves a counter behind.

A PMIC register read that fails is retried up to 3 times, and each failure soft-resets the SP's own I2C master (driver/pmic_controller.c:254-300, i2c_soft_reset at :273; driver/i2c_controller.c:406-431). The PMIC itself is not written.

GET_MODULE_MANUFACTURE_NAME.handler: services/asset_track.c:18 -> services/asset_track_mgmt.c:27 -> driver/flashfs.c:1508 (RAM copy of the flash config)

GET_MODULE_PART_NUMBER.handler: services/asset_track.c:23 -> driver/flashfs.c:1536-1541 (RAM copy of the persistent config)

GET_MODULE_SERIAL_NUMBER.handler: services/asset_track.c:34 -> services/asset_track_mgmt.c:42-48 -> driver/bl2_otp.c:252-263 (memory-mapped eFuse read of the ECID)
GET_MODULE_SERIAL_NUMBER.note: A per-die identifier read with no write: a read-only way to tell two cards' nodes apart. Compare it inside a run; never commit the value.

GET_MODULE_DRIVER_REVISION.handler: dispatched to asset tracking (rtos_task/command_dispatcher.c:136), which has no case for it: ERROR 'Unsupported Message ID' (services/asset_track.c:214), so one SP_RUNTIME_ERROR event

GET_MODULE_PCIE_ADDR.handler: as GET_MODULE_DRIVER_REVISION: no case in services/asset_track.c, ERROR at :214

SET_MODULE_PART_NUMBER.handler: services/asset_track.c:28 -> driver/flashfs.c:1563 (writes the persistent config to SPI flash)

GET_MODULE_FIRMWARE_REVISIONS.handler: services/firmware_update.c:862-915; :903 pmic_get_fw_version -> driver/pmic_controller.c:952-974 -> pmic_get_active_boot_slot :2531-2557 (set_pmic_reg(PMIC_I2C_FW_MGMTCMD_ADDRESS 0x16, ACTIVE_SLOT 7) at :2543, data read at :2549) and pmic_fw_update_subcommand :2581-2600 (set_pmic_reg(0x16, VERSION 5 | slot) at :2587, data read at :2591)
GET_MODULE_FIRMWARE_REVISIONS.what: Despite its name, it writes the PMIC's firmware-management command register twice (two subcommands, ACTIVE_SLOT then VERSION) and reads the answers. Nothing reaches the PMIC's configuration or its slots, but it is a PMIC command by E85 C1's standard. Card identity comes from module-uptime continuity instead (gov-prep, Q133).

SET_FIRMWARE_UPDATE.handler: services/firmware_update.c:1077-1089 -> dm_svc_firmware_update :661 (an OTA: writes the image to flash; may update the PMIC firmware)

SET_FIRMWARE_VALID.handler: dispatched to firmware_service_process_request (command_dispatcher.c:145), which has no case for it: ERROR at services/firmware_update.c:1128-1129, no reply

SET_MODULE_TEMPERATURE_THRESHOLDS.handler: services/thermal_power_monitor.c:493-521 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:638-643 (RAM, no range check in the SP; libDM refuses outside 20-125 C)
SET_MODULE_TEMPERATURE_THRESHOLDS.what: A governor move (the software temperature threshold). RAM only at this build: no flash write (gov-prep rule 8).

SET_MODULE_STATIC_TDP_LEVEL.handler: services/thermal_power_monitor.c:392-415 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:576-591 (refuses > 75 W, else one INFO log and the RAM assignment)
SET_MODULE_STATIC_TDP_LEVEL.what: A governor move (the static TDP). RAM only at this build: no flash or PMIC write (gov-prep rule 8).

side_effects: refreshes the SP's own RAM copy of the die temperature (g_pmic_power_reg.soc_temperature, thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:754) with the value just read, as its own task does every pass
GET_MODULE_CURRENT_TEMPERATURE.note: The field the reply calls pmic_sys is the PVT minion average (:739-746): no PMIC access.

GET_MODULE_TEMPERATURE_THROTTLE_STATUS.handler: dispatched to thermal_power_monitoring_process (command_dispatcher.c:152), which has no case for it: ERROR 'Unsupported message id!' (services/thermal_power_monitor.c:1025), no reply

side_effects: a raw state outside 0-3 (the enum at device-api/include/management-api/device_mgmt_api_spec.h:278-286) takes the default branch: two ERROR log lines (thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:1499 and thermal_power_monitor.c:607), so two SP_RUNTIME_ERROR events and two counts on the SP's error counter per state read (E77's F1; Q134(a): 4,228 events = 2 x 2,114 invalid-state reads on aifoundry2)
GET_MODULE_RESIDENCY_THROTTLE_STATES.note: The ettelem variants accept raw 2-6 (BL2 0.18.0/0.20.0 numbering): at 0.22.0 raw 4, 5 and 6 are no state. Read 2 and 3 only; raw 1 needs a binary that accepts it.

GET_MODULE_UPTIME.handler: services/thermal_power_monitor.c:698 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:1451-1455 (RAM, updated by the SP's task, :1406-1426)

GET_MODULE_VOLTAGE.handler: services/thermal_power_monitor.c:243 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:1010-1140: nine pmic_get_voltage calls (DDR, L2 cache, Maxion, Minion, PCIe, NoC, PCIe logic, VDDQLP, VDDQ) -> driver/pmic_controller.c:1473-1500 -> get_pmic_reg (:254-300, an I2C register read)
side_effects: refreshes the SP's RAM copy g_pmic_power_reg.module_voltage with the values read
GET_MODULE_VOLTAGE.what: Nine PMIC voltage-register reads, no PMIC write: allowed by the owner's rule of 2 Nov 2026 (read-only PMIC voltage reads).

GET_ASIC_VOLTAGE.handler: services/thermal_power_monitor.c:192 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:1142-1222: PVT voltage-monitor reads, then pmic_get_voltage(VDDQLP) and (VDDQ) at :1213 and :1215
side_effects: refreshes the SP's RAM copy g_soc_power_reg.asic_voltage
GET_ASIC_VOLTAGE.what: Two PMIC voltage-register reads, no PMIC write: allowed by the owner's rule of 2 Nov 2026.

GET_MODULE_POWER.handler: services/thermal_power_monitor.c:142 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:984-988 (RAM copy the SP's task keeps from the PMIC)

side_effects: a power state outside 0-3 logs two ERROR lines (thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:1550, thermal_power_monitor.c:659)

SET_MODULE_VOLTAGE.what: Sets a regulator's output voltage through the PMIC.

SET_THROTTLE_POWER_STATE_TEST.handler: services/thermal_power_monitor.c:1016 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:2034-2058 (reads the PMIC's average power, writes a power-status record into the SP trace)

SET_FREQUENCY.handler: services/thermal_power_monitor.c:870-935 (reprograms the NoC or minion PLL)

SET_PCIE_RETRAIN_PHY.handler: services/link_mgmt.c:474 -> :191 (a link retrain hung aifoundry1's host on 30 Sep 2026)

RESET_ETSOC.handler: services/firmware_update.c:1125 -> :45-105: if the PMIC firmware was updated, pmic_force_power_off_on() (a power cycle, driver/pmic_controller.c:2272); else the PMIC watchdog is armed (pmic_enable_wdog_timeout_reset, pmic_set_wdog_timeout_time) and pmic_force_reset() (:2298)
RESET_ETSOC.what: A card reset through the PMIC; the lab's tools/lab/et-reset sends it. Never in a run (the owner's rules of 2 Nov 2026: no power cycles, no resets).

side_effects: refreshes the SP's RAM copy of the clocks (get_soc_perf_reg()->asic_frequency)

GET_SP_STATS.handler: services/performance.c:404-466 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:2780-2784 (a copy of the RAM op_stats the SP's task keeps)

SET_STATS_RUN_CONTROL.handler: services/performance.c:546-636. With type SP and control RESET_COUNTER: Thermal_Pwr_Mgmt_Init_OP_Stats (:575 -> services/thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:2805-2880): the RAM op_stats re-initialised, pvt_hilo_reset() (:2828, writes the PVT controllers' high/low latches, driver/pvt_controller.c:1071-1081), PMIC reads (temperature :2838, average power :2874) and update_pmb_stats(true) (:2846 -> :1334-1350), which makes two PMIC writes: pmic_reset_pmb_stats (driver/pmic_controller.c:1801-1805: set_pmic_reg(PMB_RW 0x15, 0x47, 1 byte), the PMIC's stats reset), then pmic_get_pmb_stats (:1827-1832: set_pmic_reg(PMB_RW 0x15, 0x43 = PMIC_I2C_PMB_STATS_SNAPSHOT_VALUE, 4 bytes, include/pmic_hal.h:737), the snapshot command, before it reads the PMB stats back; the SP's own DM task sends that snapshot write every pass anyway, rtos_task/dm_task.c:215, update_pmb_stats(false)). And any control word WITHOUT bit 0 (TRACE_ENABLE) switches the SP's device-statistics trace OFF (performance.c:556-564 -> services/trace.c:654-661); Trace_Init at boot leaves it on. With type MM (2) the control goes to the Master Minion instead (performance.c:579-599 -> interface/mm_iface.c:413-450).
SET_STATS_RUN_CONTROL.what: Its forms write different things, so the checker names each (see 'forms'): STATS_RESET is the statistics reset (type 1, control 2: what ettelem --reset-ms / --reset-once-file sends), allowed by the owner's ruling of 31 Oct 2026. Besides the PMIC's stats reset and snapshot it re-arms the PVT latches and, because control 2 lacks TRACE_ENABLE, leaves the SP stats trace (dev_mngt_service -t SPST) off until something re-enables it (tools/claims-v3/tel/README.md, 'Deviations' 1). dev_mngt_service -t SPST:enable sends control 1 (the trace on, nothing reset), -t SPST:reset control 7 (the counters and the trace buffer reset, the trace on), -t MMST:... type 2: none of them is the ruled reset. A send whose form the checker cannot see keeps this name and is never allowed.

GET_DEVICE_ERROR_EVENTS.handler: rtos_task/command_dispatcher.c:174-178: only under TEST_EVENT_GEN, where it generates test events; otherwise nothing and no reply

SET_DM_TRACE_RUN_CONTROL.handler: services/trace.c:465-470 -> :126-165 (enables or disables the SP trace, can reset its buffer, and redirects the SP log to the UART or the trace buffer)

SET_DM_TRACE_CONFIG.handler: services/trace.c:474-479 -> :183-207 (sets the SP trace's event and filter masks and the SP log level, RAM; it stays until the next boot or set)
SET_DM_TRACE_CONFIG.what: ettelem loglevel. The boot default is event mask TRACE_EVENT_STRING, filter WARNING (Trace_Init_SP's default); 'loglevel warning' with a five-word variant restores it, but the stock ettelem maps every word but 'debug' to INFO, so it cannot.

GET_FRU.handler: services/asset_track.c:96-100 -> driver/pmic_controller.c:2412-2445 (pmic_read_fru): three PMIC register writes, once (FRU_OPS_CMD := SET_OFFSET :2419, FRU_DATA := offset 0 :2424, FRU_OPS_CMD := READ_FRU_DATA_BYTE :2431), then the FRU bytes read one at a time (get_pmic_reg :2438)
GET_FRU.what: A GET that writes PMIC command registers, like GET_MODULE_FIRMWARE_REVISIONS.

GET_VMIN_LUT.handler: services/asset_track.c:74 -> driver/flashfs.c:2073-2080 (RAM copy of the persistent config)
GET_VMIN_LUT.note: dev_mngt_service writes the LUT to dev<N>_vmin_lut.bin in its working directory (a host file).

GET_ASIC_PVT_SAMPLES.handler: the maintainer's command-74 patch of 7 Oct 2026 (held by the lab, not public): command_dispatcher.c routes 74 to thermal_power_monitoring_process -> pwr_svc_get_asic_pvt_samples; group 0 (PVT_SAMPLE_GROUP_MINSHIRE_TS) fills each entry with pvt_get_min_shire_ts_sample(idx), the public driver/pvt_controller.c:651-665 at 836a4ab -> pvt_get_ts_data :618-643: two PVT register reads per sensor (ts_individual[].sdif_data and .smpl_hilo), no write; the reply is built in a static RAM buffer and pushed to the host queue. That is the same register path GET_MODULE_CURRENT_TEMPERATURE (27, READ) reads (pvt_controller.c:618-643, 659-664)
GET_ASIC_PVT_SAMPLES.what: Per-sensor PVT temperature readings. Group 0 is a READ (above); group 6 is a WRITE and is refused by the sampler.
GET_ASIC_PVT_SAMPLES.forms_sent: group 0 only (tools/claims-v3/e89/pvt_sample.py refuses every group but 0 and 4; E144 sends 0)
GET_ASIC_PVT_SAMPLES.residual: aifoundry3's running build is not hashed and differs from the held patch in at least one respect: since 31 Oct its group 0 returns raw 12-bit codes where the held patch converts them to whole degrees, so its group-0 path is read from the nearest held source with a known divergence, the standard this table applies to every aifoundry3 command. Both held forms of that path (the converted read and a raw-code variant of the same function) read the same two registers and write none. The held patch's group 6 (pvt_hilo_reset, the latch reset) is a WRITE: never sent.
GET_ASIC_PVT_SAMPLES.classified_by: E144 (Q138), Mon 2 Nov 2026, before its first launch

STATS_RESET.sent_by: ettelem sample --reset-ms N (N > 0) and --reset-once-file in the reviewed variants that take them (tools/ettelem/ettelem.cpp:91-97, tools/claims-v3/hp/ettelem-hp/ettelem.cpp:69-76, tools/claims-v3/dv2/ettelem-dv2/ettelem.cpp:88-95: in[2] = {1 SP stats, 2 RESET_COUNTER}), and a reset option passed on to a sampler wrapper
STATS_RESET.what: The statistics reset, the one form the owner's ruling of 31 Oct 2026 allows: the SP's RAM statistics re-initialised, the PVT controllers' high/low latches re-armed (thermal_pwr_mgmt.c:2828), two PMIC writes (PMB_RW 0x15 := 0x47, the PMIC's stats reset, pmic_controller.c:1801-1805; then 0x15 := 0x43, the snapshot command, :1827-1832), and the SP stats trace switched off (control 2 lacks TRACE_ENABLE, performance.c:556-564).

SPST_TRACE_CONTROL.sent_by: dev_mngt_service -t SPST:enable|disable|to_uart|to_memory (device-management-application/src/dev_mngt_service.cc doTraceOperation: enable is on unless the last of enable/disable is disable)
SPST_TRACE_CONTROL.what: Switches the SP's device-statistics trace on (control 1) or off (control 0) through Trace_Run_Control_SP_Dev_Stats (performance.c:556-564); resets no counter and touches no PMIC. Not the ruled statistics reset: NO-GO in Q136.

SPST_RESET.sent_by: dev_mngt_service -t SPST:reset (with or without enable or disable): RESET_TRACEBUF | RESET_COUNTER, plus TRACE_ENABLE unless disabled
SPST_RESET.what: The counters reset (the same Thermal_Pwr_Mgmt_Init_OP_Stats as STATS_RESET: the PVT latches, the PMIC's stats reset and snapshot) plus the SP stats trace buffer reset (Trace_Reset_SP_Dev_Stats_Buffer) and the trace switched on (off with disable). Not the form the owner ruled on: NO-GO in Q136.

MMST_CONTROL.what: Forwarded to the Master Minion's firmware as SP2MM_CMD_MM_STATS_RUN_CONTROL (performance.c:579-599 -> interface/mm_iface.c:413-450): its statistics trace and counters; the Master Minion's handler is not in the service processor's source and was not read. NO-GO in Q136.

UNREVIEWED_VARIANT.what: an ettelem binary outside every reviewed build directory (tools.variants.*.build_dirs): what its subcommands send is not in this table. NO-GO until its source is reviewed into the table, or the runner names a reviewed source with --variant-source BUILD_DIR=SOURCE and that file's sha256 equals a reviewed variant's. Never allowed by --allow.

VARIANT_UNRESOLVED.what: an ettelem call whose binary the checker cannot resolve to a reviewed build directory (a variable set outside the scanned files, or a program that is not among them): its sends are listed as the reviewed variants', but which build runs is not visible. NO-GO until the runner names the source with --variant-source (KEY 'unresolved', a build directory or a program name; the source's sha256 must equal a reviewed variant's) or a person reads the line and records a reviewed --except. Never allowed by --allow.

UNKNOWN_SUBCOMMAND.what: an ettelem subcommand the matched reviewed variant does not have (or, for a forwarding wrapper's call, no reviewed subcommand among its words): what that binary does with it is not in this table. NO-GO. Never allowed by --allow.

TRACE_EXTRACT.what: dev_mngt_service -t <type>:extract and ettelem sptrace: no DM command; two driver ioctls (ETSOC1_IOCTL_GET_TRACE_BUFFER_SIZE, ETSOC1_IOCTL_EXTRACT_TRACE_BUFFER) copy a trace region over PCIe (devicelayer/src/DevicePcie.cpp:822-835; et-driver/et-soc1-pcie.c:1021-1077, et_ioread)

ETCFG.what: tools/etcfg: ETSOC1_IOCTL_GET_DEVICE_CONFIGURATION, a read-only driver ioctl (tools/etcfg/etcfg.c:28)

SYSFS_WRITE.what: a write into /sys (driver or PCI attributes: reset, remove, rescan, power, link). Never in a run.

SETPCI_WRITE.what: setpci with REG=VALUE: a PCI configuration-space write (a link retrain hung a host on 30 Sep 2026). setpci without '=' only reads.

MODULE_LOAD.what: modprobe, rmmod or insmod: loads or unloads a driver for every user of the host.

HOST_REBOOT.what: reboot, shutdown, poweroff, systemctl reboot|poweroff|kexec, or an outlet cycle: takes every card on the host. Never (the owner's rules of 2 Nov 2026).

DYNAMIC.what: a command named at run time (a variable, a format string, a numeric code from a variable): the checker cannot tell what is sent. NO-GO until the line is rewritten with literal commands.

dev_mngt_service.what: /opt/et/bin/dev_mngt_service, the vendor CLI (device-management-application/src/dev_mngt_service.cc at 836a4ab). -m <name> or -o <enum id> sends one command; on aifoundry1 it opens BOTH cards' nodes even with -n.
dev_mngt_service.code_option: -o N / --code=N takes the enum value of device_mgmt_api_spec.h (dev_mngt_service.cc:1513-1530); its README's numbering is stale
dev_mngt_service.trace_option: -t TYPE:op[,op...] (dev_mngt_service.cc:2224-2365): extract -> TRACE_EXTRACT (a read); disable, enable, reset, to_uart, to_memory -> SET_DM_TRACE_RUN_CONTROL for SP; for SPST and MMST a DM_CMD_SET_STATS_RUN_CONTROL whose form the checker names: SPST_TRACE_CONTROL (enable, disable, to_uart, to_memory: type 1, control 1 or 0), SPST_RESET (reset: control 7, or 6 with disable), MMST_CONTROL (type 2); MM and CM take no control (refused before anything is sent)

ettelem-dv2.build_dirs_note: build/ettelem-hpl/ holds this source, built for E64 (23 Oct 2026) and reused by later runs (E69, E80, E87, E98, E111, E119 and E126 among them; tools/claims-v3/hpl/README.md:54; tools/claims-v3/e126/E126.md:72, binary sha256 77a46171...); the source has not changed since 28 Sep 2026 (commit 8eb0e384)

threshold.note: 'threshold set' is refused before the node opens (:267-279)

ettelem-e77.note: No set and no PMIC read; Dm::get refuses any other command (:73-76).

sample.note: --reset-ms and --reset-once-file are refused at parse time (:325-329)

loglevel.note: refused before the node opens; the SET_DM_TRACE_CONFIG at :373 is unreachable
